pros: The fact that Asana is so easy to use. The user interface make it so easily to navigate through the great features it has
cons: Asana has no issues since we started using it. It has been working well. We had an issue integrating it with some tools but it was fixed
reasons_for_choosing: The pricing of Asana was cheaper than the other
reasons_for_switching: The pricing of the previous tool was expensive.

pros: Love the ease of use for setting up projects, managing projects, allowing volunteer team members to contribute and access through mobile.
cons: We are using the free version so the limits on number of team being able to access sometimes creates problems.
general_comments: Asana has been a great asset for allowing our administrators and volunteer team overseers to set up projects, manage projects, communicate with volunteers, and receiving reminders has been especially helpful.

pros: The user experience is an absolute gold standard. Managing dependencies between tasks is ultra-fluid, and the collaboration features (comments, likes, clear assignments) keep everyone from scattering. It’s the ideal tool to know precisely who is doing what, and by when.
cons: The moment I want to customize dashboards or add advanced mathematical formulas, I quickly feel limited. Moreover, the free version has become quite restrictive over time, and transitioning to paid plans is a real financial stretch for smaller structures.
general_comments: For me, the greatest benefit of Asana has been the drastic reduction in mental load. I no longer fear forgetting a detail; everything is centralized, and my team meetings have become twice as short because status tracking happens in real time.

review_title: Asana helps you organize and Stay on Task
pros: With Asana it is easy to set up tasks and collaborate on a project. You can assign work to colleagues with deadlines to keep a project moving along. Asana can be used internally or shared with outside vendors, which is great.
cons: Only con I have found is duplication of update emails, i.e., You can receive an update on a task, but also receive the same update if someone is assigning a specific task to you.
general_comments: A very useful tool that has helped my team communicate on projects, stay up to date on progress and stay organized.

pros: I like how there is alot of customization you can do when using this product. I also love how there is dynamic reporting. Theres a high level of collaboration available with this platform which I throughly enjoy!
cons: It was a bit hard to understand initially with how customizable it is! Even so, I enjoyed it much more as I built it out and tested it.
general_comments: Asana is a game-changer for staying organized and on top of things! It’s super easy to use, with flexible views like lists, boards, and calendars, so you can manage your projects in a way that works best for you. The collaboration features are a huge win—assign tasks, leave comments, and integrate with your favorite tools like Slack or Google Drive. Plus, the automation and templates save so much time. Whether you’re a solo act or part of a big team, Asana scales perfectly, keeping everyone on track. And the mobile app? Total lifesaver for staying productive on the go!
reasons_for_switching: I made the switch because I needed more customization.

pros: Easy to assign, keep tasks on track for deadlines, follow up within company and directly on the task instead of emailing or messaging and having confusion
cons: sometimes have difficulty with clients joining in

pros: Asana is easy to use and has many fields for a single task that I can add all the information I want, as well as a wide range of integrations and connections to other applications. I like it so much because it organises my work.
cons: I like it overall and hope it is possible to have it integrated with Siri or Google Assistant and Gemini soon, so everything can be organised with audio and as efficiently as possible.
general_comments: It is a great experience, and I have not stopped using it since I found it and could not find any better software for the same function.

pros: I love being able to manage all my clients and keep track of the work that I do each day. As well as the different board layouts.
cons: I don't have any complaints about Asana, it is a wonderful tool.
general_comments: I have been managing clients in Asana for a few years now and it is a great place for keeping track of client work and things I need to focus on to run my business.

review_title: Reliable Collaboration Software for Modern Teams
pros: The interface is my favorite thing which I really straightforward and easy to use and the project visualization and timeline feature us really helpful when I am planning for work.
cons: The notification system is bit overwhelming when the number of active projects gets higher and the resource management is not so robust as it should be.

review_title: I've Used Asana for Over 3 Years and Still Find It to Be a Great Tool
pros: Asana is different because it is designed for you to ladder projects into goals that ladder up into larger company goals and initiatives.
cons: Getting people to use it effectively is always a struggle, but I like how they were doing a promo that made their cert program free. They should do that more often because I don't think my team had time to take advantage of that.
general_comments: It's good. We use it often and the forms make process a lot easier. I like it's integration with Slack, but feel like there's more I could be doing with the tool.

review_title: Good task visibility for case based work.
pros: I like that tasks, deadlines and who is responsible is very visible so that I can keep a pulse on client's progress and not let anything fall through the cracks.
cons: Some of its more advanced features are not as easy to set up as you might expect, and customer support communication also can be sluggish when it comes to workflow questions.
general_comments: I can't say enough about how Asana has brought order to our visa cases by managing deadlines, sharing tasks across the consulting team and otherwise helping me keep structure around complex client work without depending on a web of sticky notes or digital reminders.

pros: Práctico e intuitivo. Con unas nociones básicas ya te puedes mover por el software.
cons: No hay un acceso directo a las plantillas. Para modificarlas, hay que crear un proyecto y entonces modificar la plantilla.
general_comments: LLevo un año trabajando con Asana y ha aumentado el rendimiento de nuestro departamento IT. Organizamos proyectos, tareas y subtareas. Nos pasamos las tareas unos a otros y nos damos prioridades. Todos sabemos qué hacer y qué hay que hacer antes que otras cosas.

review_title: Asana is useful for project management
pros: The ability to assign tasks is super helpful to get a project moving through the stages to completion.
cons: I am still unaware of a feature that allows you to prioritize all of your tasks but that could be something that is available.
general_comments: Asana has helped my team over the years, and I would recommend it to others looking for a way to keep on top of assignments.

pros: Asana makes it easy to collaborate with colleagues and get on the same page about what tasks need to be completed. I really like the email reminders you can set up.
cons: Sometimes it’s hard to understand if tagging someone will actually add them to a project or not.

review_title: Asana helps reign in task planning and management.
pros: Having a central tool for planning our daily tasks, managing our project resources and assigning tasks has helped us improve our productivity all thanks to Asana. Asana makes it easy to manage our operations by giving us very effective work management features which help us to streamline all our tasks. Working together with my teammates on our operations has been easy with the Asana digital collaboration workspace that allows us to engage each other abd share information easily during operations. Asana also helps us to easily track and monitor the flow of our tasks at each stage, allowing us to make sure that we are following our work plans accordingly.
cons: Working with Asana has been very easy and flawless since day one. It has a simple interface that allowed us to adopt it quickly even without any much training needed.
general_comments: Overall, our experience with Asana has been everything we ever hoped for when we were implementing it. We needed a tool to streamline our daily operations by helping us plan and manage our tasks effectively and Asana has given us just that. More to just planning our tasks, Asana has also made it easy for us to work collaboratively on our operations by giving us a very user-friendly and feature-loaded collaboration workspace.

pros: Eases the communication in the team and offers a follow-up of on meetings. Easy to get your hands on it.
cons: I find it a bit chaotic, especially when you're looking for information from previous meetings. The layout is a bit outdated.
general_comments: It's ok for team usage (less than 10 people) though I would recommend using another platform for meeting summary, project follow-ups.

pros: I am so in love with Asana as I can create, assign tasks, set deadlines, track progress across multiple projects for team communication, and I can also enable me to communicate with members ,mention, and share files.
cons: I Can say with everything in me that Asana has the most user friendly interface. When I was assigned task from a client to use Asana, it didn't take me unto 5 minuets to get use to the interface. That was the first time working Using Asana. And since then I have always loved using Asana to manage my projects and easily communicate with my clients for task submission.
general_comments: My overall experience with Asana was intriguing, and I highly recommend especially to new users as it is user friendly
reasons_for_switching: It was a little boring, but the Asana interface gives me that feeling to do more work

pros: Very flexible system that allows for a customized setup to fit our workflows within and between departments.
cons: Some of the more useful features require a bigger investment in a higher level plan.
general_comments: Asana has greatly helped our organization with organizing and tracking our projects, especially those involving multiple departments. Tasks now all appear in a single place and communication about each task is found in a central location without various email chains piling up and missing necessary recipients.
reasons_for_choosing: Asana had all the features we were looking for with more integration options to connect to our other business tools. Also offered great pricing for non-profits.
reasons_for_switching: Smartsheet is more complex and has a much steeper learning curve making it very difficult to get full buy-in across the organization.

pros: I love that I am able to track all my projects and have complete customization over rules, tags, sorting, and all the other necessary tracking tools Asana gives.
cons: When there are issues on Asana, the support team is not very responsive. This can be irritating as it would be nice to have a live chat option instead of submitting a support ticket.
general_comments: Overall, Asana has been a great tool to use as a project manager. I enjoy looking at my tasks and checking them off, the icons and customizations make my life more fun at work!
reasons_for_switching: I used Monday at my old position and when I moved to my current role I started using Asana.

pros: I like Asana's flexible workflows and custom fields. They're pretty useful for organizing complex projects. Once we rolled it out to the team, tasks were easier to track and prioritize.
cons: The mobile app could be better, sometimes it's kind of annoying to switch between tasks and projects on the go. We've had a few instances where the app froze or didn't sync properly.
general_comments: I've had a generally positive experience with Asana, finding it to be a solid project management tool that helps me stay organized and on top of tasks. The interface is user-friendly and easy to navigate, making it a great choice for regular use.
